verdicts.question: Has MSTC's EPR Electronic Trading & Settlement Platform been approved and launched since June 2026, and have direct buyer-to-seller certificate transfers on the CPCB portals stopped?
verdicts.problems: VERIFICATION LIMIT: no source could be checked by snippet this session (WebSearch budget exhausted at 200/200; fetches refused; proxy status check denied). Every claim below is 'not confirmed by snippet'; holds=true rests on the repo's own 29 Sep 2026 brief (docs/plan/research/epr.md, handoff/briefs-raw/epr.json, docs/plan/sources.md), which lists the CPCB EPRETP guidelines PDF, the Multibagg MSTC Q4 FY26 note (approval pending, 9 Jun 2026) and the Enviliance Apr 2026 report on epr.cpcb.gov.in going live in Feb 2026, all consistent with this answer. (1) The two load-bearing post-June claims, the MSTC Q1 FY27 transcript quotes of 14 Aug 2026 (BSE PDF) and the Business Standard 20 Sep 2026 non-ferrous piece, are corroborated by nothing else in the repo and were not confirmed by snippet; the 28 Jun 2026 plastic-portal switch-off rests on one secondary blog (Karparivartan) only. (2) Characterisation slip: the answer calls the 4% a 'CPCB charge on transaction value'; the repo's brief, from the same CPCB guidelines, describes it as the platform fee (2% from each side) of which 30% goes to CPCB. Founders should model it as a 4% round-trip exchange fee, not a CPCB levy. (3) No newer development could be searched for; a CPCB go-live notice between 20 and 30 Sep 2026 cannot be ruled out, so re-check etp.cpcb.gov.in before the 13 Oct pilot start, not only in mid-November. (4) Refined-chain fit: the decision says 'registered recycler to a PIBO'. In the founder's model the certificate-generating entity for plastic is any registered Plastic Waste Processor, which includes the PRE-PROCESSOR (PET flake and washing lines produce S4-S6 output and are PWPs), not only the S7 granule recycler; e-waste, battery, tyre and used-oil certificates likewise arise at the dismantler/battery breaker/shredder-pyrolysis/re-refiner (all pre-processor roles). Luma should record the transfer reference and price at price level L3 or L4 against whichever registered processor generated the certificate, and tag the certificate to the processing record's main-output lot (never to by-product or residual lots). No arithmetic in this answer to check; no unsourced figure found.

verdicts.question: What evidence do CPCB's verification guidelines under the 31 March 2026 plastic amendment (and Registered Environment Auditors) require from processors, and does the plastic EPR portal accept receipts without GST for purchases from informal collectors, as the e-waste portal does? Do the CPCB EPR and SWM portals accept bulk uploads or API connections?
verdicts.problems: VERIFICATION LIMIT: no snippet could be obtained this session (search budget exhausted, fetches refused), so every citation is 'not confirmed by snippet'. The core findings (REA inserted by G.S.R. 237(E); CPCB has six months, to 30 Sep 2026, to issue the recycled-content verification guideline; PAN/Aadhaar accepted when a supplier has no GST; e-invoice with IRN needed for PWP certificate generation since Apr 2025; SWM portal live 31 May 2026 with only BWG registration; no public API) are corroborated by the repo's brief and by the factory-integration and swm-2026 clusters, and the six-month arithmetic is right. It does not hold on three points. (1) The negative claim 'as of 29 September 2026 no such guideline appears on CPCB's plastic-waste guidelines page' is sourced to a page dated 2026-09-29 that could not have been opened on this machine and no snippet supports it; the deadline is today (30 Sep 2026), so this must be stated as unverified and re-checked, not asserted. (2) The bulk-upload description is misleading and the decision built on it is wrong: the answer says 'the plastic portal has a bulk-upload option for procurement or sales' and the decision has Luma export 'in the CPCB bulk-upload column layout'. The sibling factory-integration cluster, from the same Feb 2023 manual and CPCB's Nov 2022 module guidance (Q18: 'only single entries can be made in the procurement section'), finds the 'bulk upload' is a PIBO-side aggregate (two-year totals from one unregistered entity plus a PDF), not a row-wise Excel, and the 2023 SOP is for PIBO transactions. There is no PWP-side row-wise bulk layout to export to. (3) The e-invoice point omits that e-invoicing is mandatory only above Rs 5 crore turnover, so a small pre-processor or recycler must self-enable on the IRP before the portal will issue it certificates; this is a pilot onboarding step, not a footnote. Also missing: the scrap-tax cluster's finding that a registered yard buying metal scrap from an unregistered kabadiwala pays 18% GST under reverse charge (Notification 6/2024-CT(Rate), from 10 Oct 2024) with no threshold, which the whoToAsk line treats as an open CA question when the repo already has it. Refined-chain fit: evidence must attach to each processing record's main-output lot with yield and separate by-product/residual lots, because the third-party audit checklist reconciles procurement against output within installed capacity; a pre-processor (flake line) that is a registered PWP needs the same purchase-evidence set as the recycler, and the DWCC/MRF role should be able to issue the non-GST receipt with PAN/Aadhaar on behalf of informal sellers.
verdicts.correction: What the rules require today: G.S.R. 237(E) (31 Mar 2026) adds 'or Registered Environment Auditor' to the verification provisions and gives CPCB six months (to 30 Sep 2026) to issue a guideline on audit and verification of recycled content; whether that guideline has issued could not be verified this session and is an open item to check on cpcb.gov.in this week. Until it issues, the evidence standard is the existing portal and audit checklist: for each purchase the processor records supplier name, address, category, quantity, date and GSTIN, or PAN/Aadhaar where the supplier has no GST (CPCB Guidance Manual, Feb 2023, s.3.2.1), with an invoice copy; audits sample registered and unregistered suppliers and site-check receipts, transport and photos. So yes, the plastic portal accepts non-GST purchase receipts from informal collectors identified by PAN or Aadhaar, the same posture as the e-waste FAQ (23 Jan 2024: a sales receipt with the seller's name and address). Certificates, however, issue only against the processor's output sale backed by a GSTN-validated e-invoice with IRN and QR (CPCB PWP instruction sheet, Apr 2025); e-invoicing is compulsory only above Rs 5 crore turnover, so smaller pre-processors and recyclers must self-enable on the IRP first. Uploads: PWP procurement and sales are single-entry (one invoice per entry; the CEPP app scans one QR at a time); the manual's 'bulk upload' is a PIBO-side two-year aggregate per unregistered counterparty plus a PDF, and the 2023 SOP covers PIBO transactions, so there is no row-wise bulk layout for processors. No public API exists for any CPCB EPR portal (only the secured CPCB-EPRETP link), and swm.cpcb.gov.in (live 31 May 2026, BWG registration only) documents neither bulk upload nor API. Decision: record every informal purchase with seller name, address, mobile, PAN or masked Aadhaar, date, category, weight, price and receipt photo, attached to the processing record's main-output lot; capture GSTIN, IRN and e-way bill on every processor sale; export one invoice per row for an operator to key into the portal (not a bulk feed); book reverse-charge GST on registered-yard purchases of metal scrap from unregistered sellers; keep API integration out of scope. Status: partly. Who to ask: CPCB WM-III/EPR helpdesk on whether the verification guideline has issued.

verdicts.question: Are EPR regimes for non-ferrous metal scrap and for construction and demolition waste in force in 2026, and do they cover kabadiwala metal trades (copper, aluminium, brass)? What did the Delhi High Court decide on the e-waste EPR floor price (₹22/kg)? What are the current recycled-content requirements for plastic packaging after the 2024–2026 amendments?
verdicts.problems: VERIFICATION LIMIT: no snippet could be obtained this session (search budget exhausted, fetches refused), so all 19 citations are 'not confirmed by snippet'. holds=true rests on corroboration inside the repo: the 29 Sep 2026 brief lists Trilegal's July 2025 update on non-ferrous EPR, records the Blue Star stay of Dec 2025 with the main case pending in Jan 2026, the ₹22/kg floor 'reported' and in court, the recycled-content ladder (Cat I 40% in 2026-27 to 60% by 2028-29; Cat II 10% to 20%; Cat III 5% to 10%), the three-year carry-forward for food-contact shortfalls, IS 14534:2023 labelling, and the Centre's power to relax hazardous-waste timelines by up to nine months; all match this answer. Not corroborated anywhere in the repo and therefore open: the non-ferrous target ladder (10/30/50/75%) and recycled-content minimums (5% to 10/20/25%), the 1,000-tonne bulk-consumer threshold, the C&D thresholds (20,000 sq m; 25% to 100%; 5% to 25%), the cdwm.cpcb.gov.in 'dashboard showing zeros' (a page that could not have been opened here), the 8 Jul 2025 and 13 Jun 2026 court-status reports, and the ₹5.9/kg reverse-auction figure (single Newslaundry report). The court status is dated 13 Jun 2026; a judgment or further order between June and 30 Sep 2026 could not be searched for, so the decision to hold ₹22/kg should carry a re-check date. Small wording issue: the ₹22/kg floor applies to consumer electronics; other categories (e.g. smartphones) have different floors, which the answer does not say. Arithmetic (five-year non-ferrous ladder, four-year plastic ladders) is internally consistent. Refined-chain fit: (a) the non-ferrous regime touches more of the founder's roles than the kabadiwala: the yard, cable granulator, aluminium/copper pre-processor and e-waste dismantler are 'collection agents' or 'recyclers' under Chapter VIII and will need portal registration once it opens, so the 'non-ferrous EPR-relevant' tag must apply to every S1-S4 metal lot in the chain, and ferrous lots must be tagged out; (b) brass is covered as a copper-zinc alloy, so brass by-product lots (dross, turnings) from the industrial by-product list inherit the tag; (c) 'leave C&D out of scope' is right for kabadiwala trades but the founder lists C&D crushers as a pre-processor role: a crusher partner is a registered C&D recycler on cdwm.cpcb.gov.in whose recycled-aggregate output (S4-S7) sells at L3/L4 to builders bound by the 5% recycled-materials rule, so C&D lots should be recordable even though no kabadiwala certificate exists; (d) the e-waste floor applies to certificates generated by the dismantler/recycler (pre-processor tier), so any revenue assumption belongs at L3, not at the kabadiwala's L1/L2 price.
